answer.rationale: Two of three concurrent problems (activation down, onboarding completion down) are directly addressed by onboarding simplification, which has durable supporting evidence from two independent inherited memories (memory_31, memory_86) showing lasting activation gains without noted retention harm. Promotional_pricing is tempting given competitor pressure, but memory_73 explicitly warns that steep discounting boosts short-term signups while eroding retention and masking underlying product gaps—exactly the failure mode to avoid when the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue. I verify memory_73 to confirm the discount risk still applies before ruling it out, and memory_31 to confirm the onboarding evidence is solid before committing the week's only experiment slot. I'm not going to broad rollout because the current activation/onboarding dip could partly stem from competitive dynamics rather than pure funnel friction, so a standard experiment lets us measure impact before wider commitment. Pricing competition is left unaddressed this cycle by design, since a defensive discount response risks the same retention erosion previously observed.
